title: eludite.browser.input output
description: What was done and where it landed.

tab.description: The tab the command acted on.

target.description: The element the action landed on (for a point, the element there; for `type` and `key` without a target, the focused element) and the point in CSS pixels of the viewport. `ref` is in the page generation from before the action.

page_generation.description: The tab's page generation: it grows when the main frame navigates or the document is replaced (DOM.documentUpdated). Refs are valid only in the generation that issued them.

navigated.description: The main frame navigated within `wait_ms` (refs from before are stale).

url.description: The page's url when it navigated.

console_errors.description: Console errors (console.error, uncaught exceptions, failed loads the browser logged) emitted during the action, oldest first.

stack.description: For exceptions: the stack, one `at function (url:line:column)` per line.

dialog.description: The action opened a dialog the page now waits on (the action's events were delivered; the page is paused until it is answered). Answer it with eludite.browser.dialog.

kind.description: `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt` (JavaScript), `beforeunload` (the page asks to confirm leaving), `file` (a file chooser), `auth` (an HTTP authentication challenge), `permission` (the page asks for geolocation, notifications, the camera, ...).

paused.description: Present (true) when the page stopped in the debugger during the action: a breakpoint, a `debugger` statement or an exception in a browser debugging session (brief 0038). The action's events were delivered up to the stop and the page runs no script until the session continues; read the stop with eludite.debug.wait or eludite.debug.state.
